items.text: Claude GitHub App installed on ck5o4/multifamily with write access - cloud push unblocked
items.why: FIXED 2026-08-17 by Anthony. Root cause was subtler than 'a missing scope': the Claude app was AUTHORIZED on ck5o4 but INSTALLED only on the flux-brain-hq org, never on the personal account that owns multifamily. Authorization is what let cloud sessions read; installation is what grants repo Contents:write, so every push 403'd while every read succeeded - exactly the observed asymmetry. Installed via github.com/apps/claude/installations/new -> ck5o4 -> Only select repositories -> multifamily. Verified at installation 154488689: 'Read and write access to ... code' and 'Selected 1 repository: ck5o4/multifamily'. Scoped to that one repo deliberately. NOTE: the post-install redirect lands on claude.ai/admin-settings/... which shows 'You don't have access to organization settings' on a personal plan - that dead end is cosmetic, not a failure. CONFIRMED 2026-08-18 PM: the scheduled cloud sweep pushed to origin/main for real (3254356..feb4e3a). No 403, no recovery-patch email. TRAP FOR FUTURE SWEEPS: the cloud container starts on a DETACHED HEAD with the local 'main' ref left at a stale commit, so 'git push -u origin main' fails with 'behind its remote' and reads exactly like the old permissions failure. It is not. Fix is 'git branch -f main HEAD && git checkout main' before pushing, or push HEAD:main. SECOND HALF OF THE TRAP, found 2026-08-18: the stale ref is not just local 'main' - the remote-tracking ref 'origin/main' is ALSO stale on container start. This run opened with 'git log origin/main..HEAD' listing 9 commits that looked unpushed (including work already confirmed pushed on 08-18 PM). They were not unpushed; the container's cached origin/main simply predated them. A single 'git fetch origin main' moved origin/main ccdf19f..f38b13b and the list went empty. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUTINE: step 4 tells the scan to judge the git-push-rule todo by whether 'git log origin/main..HEAD' is empty, so ALWAYS fetch before running that test - otherwise a clean repo reads as 9 commits of lost work and the scan will 'recover' work that was never lost.

items.why: Found 2026-09-06; escalated 2026-09-07 (now THREE fires in one day). Two runs swept the identical window today: one at ~12:00 UTC that created digest draft r5771603367285783142 at 13:10:44Z, and a second at ~13:10 UTC that found the draft already there. Same pattern on 09-02 and 09-04, each of which has TWO unsent drafts titled 'Deal Flow digest - <date> (PM)'. Cost is not just duplicate drafts: the 12:00 run's digest carried two false statements that the second run had to repair - it claimed all digests since ~Aug 18 had empty bodies (false, every one is 2,008-4,925 chars) and it told Anthony to write a Rider reply from scratch, supplying suggested text, when draft r1750751368094010186 has held substantively that same reply since 2026-08-18. That is the 'verify before instructing' rule failing inside the routine itself. Fix: list the account's Routines, keep one Deal Flow sweep, delete the duplicate. UPDATE 2026-09-07 23:15 UTC: three fires today, not two - 00:09 (AM digest r-3531512889927791335), 13:23 (PM digest r-8315775485061088736) and 23:11. The 23:11 run repaired the 13:23 draft rather than duplicating it, and had to undo the same class of defect as on 09-06: the 13:23 digest told Anthony to 'find the correct broker contact' for Beau Box when bgarrett@beaubox.com was found 2026-08-17 and draft r5125392449427038899 has been ready since 2026-08-09, it omitted the Rider reply (r1750751368094010186, unsent 20 days) and the Hernandez request (r6910164296570484338, never sent) entirely, and it inverted the Vercher silence - Vercher answered 2026-08-03, the 35 days of silence are Anthony's. Second consecutive day an extra firing produced false instructions a later run had to repair. This is now a correctness problem, not a tidiness one. CORRECTED 2026-09-08 13:20 UTC (email sweep) - THE PREMISE OF THIS ITEM WAS WRONG. This run listed the account's Routines directly instead of inferring from draft timestamps. There is exactly ONE Deal Flow sweep routine: trig_01HJCstYwuekG3WoFodSwAQB, 'Deal Flow email sweep + board update', cron '0 13,23 * * *', enabled, created 2026-08-09, never updated since. has_more=false; the only other routines on the account are the weekly bug sweep (0 3 * * 1) and the daily scan (0 14 * * *). So TWO fires per day is the configured schedule, not a duplicate, and the fix recorded here for three days - 'list the account's Routines, keep one, delete the duplicate' - is not actionable because there is no duplicate to delete. Anthony would have gone looking for a second routine and found nothing. That is this repo's own 'verify before instructing' rule failing inside a todo, which is the same defect class the item was created to track. WHAT REMAINS UNEXPLAINED: the ~00:09 UTC digest drafts on 09-07 (r-3531512889927791335) and 09-08 (r-5393488354865663425) match neither cron hour. Most likely they are the 23:0x fire running long and creating its draft after midnight UTC, but this run could not prove that and is not asserting it. The 13:23/13:17 and 23:11 fires are simply the schedule. WHAT TO ACTUALLY DECIDE: two sweeps a day is a cadence choice, not a bug. It is only harmful when a run with no new mail invents urgency, which is what happened 09-06 and 09-07. The prompt already guards this ('No signal = no draft') and the guard held on both fires today - the 00:09 AM digest was accurate and this 13:17 run added no duplicate. If Anthony wants one sweep a day, change the cron to '0 13 * * *' on the trigger above; an unattended run should not halve his inbox coverage on its own, so that stays his call. Reclassified from 'de-duplicate it' to 'decide the cadence'. NEW EVIDENCE 2026-09-11 13:1x UTC (email sweep), and it closes the 'unexplained ~00:09 draft' question above: the 2026-09-10 PM fire produced TWO digest drafts 55 minutes apart - r7426230499633812158 at 23:15:08Z (subject 'Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-10 (PM)', 5,013 chars, recipient ridgebackpeak@gmail.com) and r2145619574996706100 at 2026-09-11T00:10:20Z (subject 'Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-11 (PM)', 5,629 chars). Both cover the identical window and the identical three CHECK listings (Olympia, Kabel, E Boyd), so this IS the 23:00 fire running long and writing its draft after UTC midnight - exactly the hypothesis this item declined to assert on 09-08, now supported by two drafts from one fire. TWO NEW DEFECTS IN THAT LATE DRAFT, both found and fixed this run: (1) it had NO RECIPIENT AT ALL - toRecipients was absent, so the digest could not be sent, only read in the Drafts folder; (2) because UTC had rolled over, it was titled '2026-09-11 (PM)', which is TODAY's date - a digest labelled for a day it does not cover, sitting in the folder before today's sweep ran, is a trap: it invites a later run or Anthony to believe the 09-11 PM sweep already happened. Fixed by adding the recipient and retitling to 'Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-10 (PM, full triage)'. The BODY WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED - update_draft merge semantics preserve an omitted body, and this repo has already recorded two separate incidents of a body rewrite introducing a worse defect than the one it fixed, so only 'to' and 'subject' were passed. Its first body line still reads '2026-09-11 (PM)'; that is known and left alone on purpose. NOTE the draft-count cost is now visible: FOUR digest drafts exist for 2026-09-10 alone (13:19, 13:23, 23:15, 00:10). STANDING CHECK FOR FUTURE SWEEPS: after creating a digest draft, re-read it and confirm toRecipients is populated - a digest with no recipient reads as a normal draft in every listing that omits the recipient field, which is how this one survived a full day unnoticed. Cadence decision itself is still Anthony's and still unmade. NEW EVIDENCE 2026-09-15 13:1x UTC (email sweep): the 13:00 slot double-fired again, and this time the two fires are only ~80 seconds apart. Digest draft r2422665991899815004 ('Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-15 (PM)', recipient present, 2,9xx chars) was created at 13:09:04Z by one session; the routine's last_run then shows fired_at 2026-09-15T13:10:24Z for a SECOND session (cse_01Hck9R1aNDXEoWJHJgZQRwP), which is this run. Same shape as 09-14 (13:21 + 13:22), 09-11 (13:18 + 13:22) and 09-10 (13:19 + 13:23). So there are now TWO distinct duplication mechanisms on record, and they are not the same thing: (a) the 23:00 fire running long and writing its draft after UTC midnight (established 2026-09-11, produces the ~00:0x drafts and the wrong-date titles), and (b) the 13:00 slot firing twice within a few minutes, which cron '0 13,23' does not explain and which a single long-running session does not explain either. Mechanism (b) is the one still undiagnosed. This run did NOT create a second digest: the 13:09 draft was re-read in full and independently re-verified against the mailbox and the repo (Sent, inbox, deal-intake/) and its contents are correct, so per the prompt's 'No signal = no draft' guard nothing was added. The guard is working - it is what keeps mechanism (b) from costing a duplicate draft every day. One cosmetic defect in the 13:09 draft, left unrepaired on purpose: its header line reads 'Run: ~20:00 UTC' when the draft was created at 13:09 UTC. It misstates only the run time, no action item and no mailbox fact, and this repo has recorded two incidents of a body rewrite introducing a worse defect than the one it fixed, so the body was not touched. Cadence decision is still Anthony's and still unmade. NEW EVIDENCE 2026-09-17 (PM sweep): the 13:00 slot double-fired again, ~2 minutes apart. A sibling session created digest draft r-6187333713441439342 ('Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-17 (PM)', recipient present) at 13:10:11Z; this session's own clock check ran 13:10:06Z. Mechanism (b) therefore persists and is still undiagnosed. Per the standing precedent this run did NOT create a duplicate digest - it re-read the sibling draft in full and corrected it in place. BUT the guard 'no duplicate draft' is not the same as 'no harm': the sibling's digest carried the false claim 'No external drafts pending' and told Anthony to consider writing fresh outreach to Rider, Vercher or Hernandez, when four finished drafts have been unsent for 12-31 days. That is the fourth recorded instance of an extra 13:00 firing producing a false instruction a later run had to repair (09-06, 09-07, 09-14, 09-17), and it is the SAME defect class each time: a run asserting draft state without querying drafts by recipient. Cadence decision is still Anthony's and still unmade, but the evidence now favours one fire a day: every extra firing so far has cost a correction, not caught anything new.

items.why: NEW 2026-09-09 AM (email sweep), from a Crexi saved-search alert 2026-09-08 19:57 UTC. HAND SCREEN, ESTIMATED BASIS, STATED AS SUCH: Kenner 70062 3BR house rents run $1,400-2,000 with the single-family median ~$1,850; at a deliberately conservative $1,600/mo x 3 = $57,600 GPR, 7pct vacancy, Jefferson insurance $3,000/unit wind, Jefferson millage 118.40, mgmt 9pct, and the CLAUDE.md per-unit expense lines with utilities tenant-paid, NOI is ~$29.7K at ask = 7.38pct cap, and DSCR at 75pct LTV / ~7pct / 25yr is 1.147 - UNDER the 1.30 house floor. Whether ~$361K also clears the 13pct IRR / beats-the-index band has NOT been run and needs the real solver on verified rents. Open items before any offer, in order: (1) actual leases or a rent roll - the $1,600 is a market estimate off listing sites, which is exactly the Treme trap; (2) bindable Jefferson wind insurance quote - $3,000/unit is assumed, and per the 2026-08-17 metro/inland finding the insurance quote, not capital, is what binds metro deals at this size; (3) run flood.py - Kenner is Jefferson and much of it sits behind levees; (4) condition/vintage on all three houses (vintage capex was the bug that killed Baker and Treme on re-screen); (5) the management-economics caveat from CLAUDE.md applies hard here - 3 SCATTERED DETACHED doors is the thinnest possible third-party-management profile, worse than 3 units in one building, and per-deal closing/loan/insurance minimums spread over only 3 doors. items.text: marketwatch snapshot creates a dated folder even when every fetch fails, masking staleness
items.why:
FOUND 2026-09-12 (daily scan). tools/marketwatch.py snapshot() calls snapdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) at line 179, BEFORE any fetch is attempted, and prints 'snapshot saved -> <dir>' at line 200 unconditionally. This run every one of the four comp fetches failed with http 000 (blocked by the cloud egress policy - see network-policy), yet market-data/snapshots/2026-09-12/ was still created and is EMPTY (0 files), and the command exited 0. CONSEQUENCE: the step-3 staleness check reads the age of the newest folder under market-data/snapshots/, so from tomorrow that empty folder reads as a fresh snapshot and suppresses the next 7 days of snapshot attempts - the staleness signal is destroyed by the failure it should have surfaced. MITIGATING FACT, verified: observations.jsonl is honest - the four rows were written as {"ok": false, "http": "000"} rather than as zero-unit rows, so no fake 'everything leased' velocity was recorded and marketwatch.py assumptions correctly reports '(no structured price observations yet)'. The corruption is confined to the directory-age heuristic. MITIGATED THIS RUN, NOT FIXED: the empty directory market-data/snapshots/2026-09-12/ was removed in-run with rmdir, which is what earlier blocked scans (08-24 through 09-04) also did, so tomorrow's staleness check still sees 2026-08-17 as the newest real snapshot and the cadence is not suppressed. Note this cleanup is the ONLY thing standing between a failed snapshot and a corrupted staleness signal, and it depends on each run remembering to do it - git does not track empty directories, so the bad state never reaches the repo but also never self-heals if a run forgets. CODE FIX STILL OWED (deliberately not applied this run - an unattended scan should not silently patch its own tooling): have snapshot() remove its directory when it ends up empty, and print FAIL / exit non-zero when no comp fetch succeeded, so a fully-failed snapshot cannot be reported as 'snapshot saved' or mistaken for a fresh one. REPRODUCED AND RE-MITIGATED 2026-09-13 (daily scan), second consecutive day. 'python3 tools/marketwatch.py snapshot' printed FAIL for all four comps (http 000), then still printed 'snapshot saved -> /home/user/multifamily/market-data/snapshots/2026-09-13' and EXITED 0, creating a 0-file directory - exactly the behaviour described when this was found. The directory was removed in-run with rmdir, so the newest real snapshot remains 2026-08-17 and tomorrow's staleness check is not suppressed. observations.jsonl again behaved honestly, recording four {"ok": false, "http": "000"} rows, and 'marketwatch.py assumptions' correctly reported '(no structured price observations yet)' with 3 heuristic rows excluded - so no fake rent or velocity data entered the record. CODE FIX STILL OWED and still deliberately not applied by an unattended scan: have snapshot() rmdir its own directory when empty and exit non-zero when every fetch fails. Until then the staleness signal survives only because each blocked run remembers to clean up by hand. REPRODUCED AND RE-MITIGATED 2026-09-14 (daily scan), THIRD consecutive day. 'python3 tools/marketwatch.py snapshot' printed FAIL for all four comps (http 000), then still printed 'snapshot saved -> .../market-data/snapshots/2026-09-14' and EXITED 0, creating a 0-file directory. This now needs an attended session to land the one-line fix; three days of hand-cleanup is the evidence that it should stop being hand-cleaned. FIXED 2026-09-15 (daily scan). cmd_snapshot() now counts successful fetches: on 0 of N it removes the empty dated dir, prints 'SNAPSHOT FAILED: 0 of N comps fetched - nothing saved', and exits 1; on partial success it prints '(got of N comps)' so a degraded snapshot is no longer indistinguishable from a clean one. Fixed in-run: git checkout -B main <commit> then push; origin/main advanced a0263dc..525c4bd and the tree is clean. THE REAL TRAP, and the reason this is written down: the push failure was invisible to the shell check. 'git push ... 2>&1 | tail -5; echo EXIT=$?' printed EXIT=0, because $? reports the exit status of TAIL, not of git. A run that trusts that number will report a successful push to Anthony while the commit is stranded in a detached HEAD that the next container throws away. STANDING RULE for every routine that commits: never confirm a push from an exit code taken through a pipe. Confirm it by comparing refs - 'git fetch origin main && git rev-parse origin/main' must equal 'git rev-parse HEAD' - and check 'git status -sb' does not say '(no branch)' BEFORE committing. Closes when the routines that push (email sweep, daily scan) do that ref comparison as their push check. RECURRED 2026-09-20 (daily scan) - second consecutive container, same signature. 'git status -sb'
read '## HEAD (no branch)' ('HEAD detached from refs/heads/main') at container start, with the local
'main' ref stale at 113792c. This run applied the rule recorded here BEFORE committing anything:
(1) 'git fetch origin main' first, which moved origin/main 113792c..c4d964f - confirming again that the
container's cached origin/main is stale on start, so 'git log origin/main..HEAD' is meaningless until
after a fetch; (2) reattached with 'git branch -f main HEAD && git checkout main', which reported
'Switched to branch main' / 'up to date with origin/main'; (3) verified the push by REF COMPARISON, not
by an exit code through a pipe. Worth noting the ordering hazard: had this run trusted the pre-fetch
'git log origin/main..HEAD' (empty) it would have been right by luck, since HEAD already equalled
origin/main - on a container whose cached ref was further behind, the same empty result would have been a
false 'nothing to push'. Item stays OPEN: it closes only when the routine prompts themselves carry the
ref-comparison push check, and an unattended run should not rewrite its own schedule. RECURRED 2026-09-21 (daily scan), and this was the WORST-DRIFT instance recorded so far. The container
opened on a DETACHED HEAD at 249a19a ('HEAD detached from refs/heads/main') while the local 'main' ref
sat stale at 113792c - TWENTY commits behind origin/main, versus the eight-commit gap logged on
2026-09-20. Had this run committed and pushed without looking, it would have committed off-branch and
then pushed the stale main ref, reproducing the 09-20 rejection exactly. Handled in the documented
order: (1) 'git fetch origin main' FIRST, which moved origin/main 113792c..249a19a - so the pre-fetch
unpushed list was computed against a 20-commit-stale ref and any 'nothing to push' read from it would
have been meaningless; (2) reattached with 'git checkout -B main origin/main', which reported
"branch 'main' set up to track 'origin/main'" / 'Your branch is up to date', with all working-tree
modifications preserved; (3) verified HEAD == origin/main == 249a19a by REF COMPARISON before
committing, and verified the day's push the same way afterwards - never by an exit code read through a
pipe, which the 09-20 entry showed reports 0 for the tail, not for git. Item stays OPEN: it closes only
when the routine prompts themselves carry the fetch-first + ref-comparison push check, and an unattended
run should not rewrite its own schedule. TRAP FIRED AND WAS CAUGHT 2026-09-22: this container started in detached HEAD ('fatal: HEAD does not point to a branch') and 'git log origin/main..HEAD' showed 22 unpushed commits back to 2026-09-15 - which was a STALE remote-tracking ref, not lost work. After 'git fetch origin main', origin/main advanced 113792c -> 8d3fdc1 (== HEAD) and both ahead/behind counts went to 0. Confirms the standing rule: always fetch BEFORE judging whether a push landed, never trust the local origin/main in a fresh cloud container. RECURRED 2026-09-23 (daily scan) - fourth consecutive run starting detached. 'git branch --show-current' printed nothing and 'git status -sb' printed '## HEAD (no branch)'. HEAD was e971a91, which DID equal origin/main after 'git fetch origin main' (86a66ca..e971a91), but the local 'main' ref was stale at 86a66ca - two commits behind. Pushing 'main' from that state would have pushed the stale ref and been rejected, exactly the 2026-09-20 trap. Handled the same documented way BEFORE committing rather than after: 'git checkout -B main e971a91' reattached the branch at the correct commit, after which 'git status -sb' read '## main...origin/main' with the working-tree changes intact. The commit and push for this scan were then made on a real branch. The container keeps opening detached, so this check stays mandatory at the START of every run, and the push must still be verified by comparing rev-parse HEAD to rev-parse origin/main afterwards - never by \$? on a piped git push. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-24: the container again started in DETACHED HEAD ('HEAD detached at refs/heads/main'), but this time HEAD and origin/main were the same commit (5e1ee5c) with git log origin/main..HEAD empty, so nothing was stranded. Push verified by git rev-parse comparison, not by a piped exit code. RECURRED 2026-09-25 (daily scan) - the signature is now unbroken since 09-20. items.text: ONE Deal Flow firing spawned TWO concurrent sweep sessions - duplicate digest drafts, live risk of racing pushes
items.why:
FOUND 2026-09-21 (13:00 UTC email sweep). This is NOT the same thing as todo sweep-double-fire, which is about the cron being 0 13,23 (two SCHEDULED firings a day, by design). This is one scheduled firing producing two SIMULTANEOUS sessions. Evidence, all verified in-run: list_triggers shows exactly one Deal Flow routine (trig_01HJCstYwuekG3WoFodSwAQB, cron '0 13,23'), so there is no duplicate routine; that trigger's run record shows scheduled_for 2026-09-21T13:07:57Z but last_fired_at 13:14:43Z - a ~7 minute gap consistent with the scheduler RETRYING a firing whose first session was in fact alive and working. At 13:15:39Z, 57 seconds into this (retry) session and before it had written anything, a draft 'Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-21 (PM)' (id r-419617508088020594) appeared that this session did not create. Its body describes fresh in-run verification, so the first session completed a full sweep. Both sessions reached the same conclusion (0 new listings, 0 broker replies, no sends), so nothing was corrupted TODAY only because neither had a reason to commit. THE RISK worth writing down: if a firing like this lands on a day where todos.json DOES change, two sessions run tools/board.py, republish the same artifact url, and push to main concurrently - the second push is rejected (or worse, a run 'fixes' it with checkout -B and strands the other's commit, cf. todo detached-head-push). Prior evidence this recurs: drafts exist at 2026-09-17T13:11:53Z, 13:11:54Z AND 13:13:31Z (three in 98 seconds) and at 2026-09-14T13:21:46Z + 13:22:02Z - same duplicate-session signature, previously unexplained. SECONDARY DEFECT, same draft: it is titled '(PM)' though it ran at 13:15 UTC, which is the AM firing (the 09-20 commit calls 13:xx AM and 23:xx PM), and it reports Rampart/Stirling/Beau Box as 'stalled outreach - NEW FLAGS (missed by prior sweeps)' when todo distribution-drafts has tracked exactly those three since 2026-08. Anthony may read that as new work; it is not. FIX: give the sweep a start-of-run guard - before doing anything, search drafts for subject 'Deal Flow digest - <today>' and, if one already exists from a session that is not this one, stop and do not duplicate the digest, the board republish or the commit. Closes when that guard is in the routine prompt.

RECURRED 2026-09-22, AND THIS TIME IT PRODUCED A FALSE INSTRUCTION (found by the evening sweep, 23:0x UTC). The single 13:00 UTC firing again spawned two sessions. Session A wrote draft r-1975393305912418924 at 13:11 UTC, titled 'Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-22 (AM, 13:00 UTC)'. Session B wrote draft r-6408430922714877880 at 13:19 UTC and titled it '(PM)' - which was WRONG on its face, since it was written at 13:13 UTC and covers the same 13:00 window. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS, both corrected by the evening sweep: (1) MISLABELLING. Session B's '(PM)' title claimed the evening slot that this sweep actually fills. Had it been left alone, Anthony would have opened a draft labelled PM that does not cover the evening window at all and never mentions the only listing that arrived in it (1350 Magazine St, 17:03 UTC). Retitled to '(13:00 UTC window - DUPLICATE RUN, see correction)' and the evening window appended to it, rather than creating a third digest for a window with no signal. (2) THE METADATA-READ FALSE ALARM AGAIN - third recorded instance. Session B's footer asserted: 'AM draft at 13:11 UTC had empty body (prior run didn't complete). This PM draft supersedes it.' THAT IS FALSE. Draft r-1975393305912418924 was retrieved with get_draft PLAIN_TEXT this evening and is complete and substantive - full DSCR break-even ($1,105/unit/mo) and price ladder ($390K/$351K/$312K) on 1346/1356 Main St, the Toulouse STR caveat, and the five-draft stalled-outreach list. Session B's own digest is the WEAKER of the two: it flags Main St as 'CHECK' without doing the arithmetic. So a run declared the better digest empty and told Anthony its own thinner one superseded it. Footer removed and replaced with a pointer to r-1975393305912418924 as the one to read. ROOT CAUSE is the same one already recorded twice under vercher-reply: list_drafts defaults to a METADATA-ONLY view that returns no body, and a run reading only that view concludes the draft is empty. STANDING RULE, NOW THIRD-EARNED AND IT APPLIES TO DIGESTS TOO, NOT JUST BROKER DRAFTS: never characterise ANY draft - including another sweep session's digest - from list_drafts metadata. Call get_draft with PLAIN_TEXT or FULL_CONTENT and read the body first. Never write 'supersedes', 'empty', or 'delete it' about a draft you have not read in full. CADENCE NOTE for whoever resolves sweep-double-fire: the duplicate is not just wasted tokens - the two sessions do not see each other, so the second one narrates the first as broken. Until one firing produces one session, every sweep must check for a same-window sibling digest BEFORE writing or judging one.

items.text: board.py emits a HEADLESS HTML fragment - the published board depends on a wrapper that is not in the repo
items.why: FOUND 2026-09-25 (daily scan). tools/board.py writes portfolio/board.html starting at '' and ending at '</div>': no <!doctype>, no <html>/<head>/<body>, and critically NO viewport meta. The live published page at the standing artifact link is NOT that file - it is that fragment wrapped in 537 bytes of prefix and 16 bytes of suffix: '<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset=utf8><meta name=viewport content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1,viewport-fit=cover"><style>:root{color-scheme:light;...padding-top:env(safe-area-inset-top,0px)...}</style></head><body>' + fragment + '</body></html>'. Verified by diffing the live page against 'git show HEAD:portfolio/board.html': 14 diff lines, ALL of them that wrapper, zero substantive differences - so the board content itself has never diverged from the generator. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) Publishing portfolio/board.html directly would drop the viewport meta and the safe-area padding, which is exactly the CSS that makes the board readable on a phone - and the phone is how the standing link is actually read. (2) Every republish now costs a merge: the Artifact tool refuses a publish to an artifact this session has not read, and the saved live copy has to be re-split into prefix/fragment/suffix and recombined with today's board before publishing. This run did that merge by hand (published 210,429 bytes, Version 61) and the wrapper survived intact. UNRESOLVED PROVENANCE, stated rather than guessed: it is not established whether that wrapper is added automatically by the artifact publishing pipeline when handed a fragment, or was hand-written by an earlier run. Either way the repo does not contain it, so it is one bad merge away from being lost silently. FIX, one place: make tools/board.py emit a complete document - doctype, <html>, <head> with charset + 'width=device-width,initial-scale=1,viewport-fit=cover', <body> - so the file on disk IS the page and no out-of-repo wrapper is load-bearing. Do that from a local session where the rendered result can be eyeballed on a phone; an unattended run should not restructure the generator's output and then publish it unseen. Closes when board.py's own output opens with <!doctype html> and carries the viewport meta.
